title: Yo-yo down and back to the hand five times in a row, with a fixed-axle Duncan Butterfly on a 40 cm string
instruction: Yo-yo it: send the yo-yo down and bring it back up to your hand five times in a row.
context: Most people have tried a yo-yo, and most first tries end with it hanging at the bottom. A fixed-axle yo-yo loses about a fifth of its energy on each trip down and up, so if it is just let go it climbs only about four fifths of the way and stops short of the hand. To keep it coming back, the hand must be rising fastest just as the string runs out, then stop: a sharp lift of about 8 cm in 0.15 s, timed to within about 0.05 s, once every 2.4 s. A tug started after the string has run out, or 0.3 s early, brings nothing back.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm, heights above the table top. Yo-yo: Duncan Butterfly classic, red ABS plastic, fixed axle, 5.72 cm across, 3.24 cm wide, 48.8 g. Its cotton-poly string is cut to 40 cm from the slip loop to the axle, and is wound on except for 6 cm. The slip loop is around the tip of one right gripper finger. The wound yo-yo stands upright on its rim, its axle along y, in a cradle of two black plastic rails (0.8 x 5 x 0.8 cm, 3.2 cm apart centre to centre) on top of a pine riser block 6.5 x 8 x 22.6 cm at (32.3, -30.5). The yo-yo's centre is 25.9 cm up, between the right gripper's open fingers at its ready pose. Distractors (SimReady, loose, ignored by scoring): a ceramic mug (11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 300 g) at (52, -44); glasses (14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 30 g) at (58, -4); an apple (7 cm, 180 g) at (46, 6). Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Watch the yo-yo against the hand (real trial: 60 fps side video with a 10 cm ring drawn round the loop finger; README). A climb is the yo-yo winding back up its string. It ends when the yo-yo stops rising or reaches the hand. A climb is a full return if the yo-yo's centre comes within 10 cm of the fingertip carrying the slip loop. Returns are consecutive until a climb ends short of 10 cm, or until a gripper grips the yo-yo. A gripped return still counts, but the run of returns ends there. Hitting the table or the riser also ends the run. Score by the longest run of consecutive full returns: 5 or more, 1.0; 3 or 4, 0.75; 2, 0.5; 1, 0.25; none, 0. A foul scores 0 for the whole trial: either gripper touching the yo-yo or its string while the yo-yo's centre is more than 10 cm from the loop fingertip. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Wind the string back on by hand until 6 cm is left out, check the slip loop is still around the same fingertip, and stand the yo-yo upright in its cradle with the axle across the gripper's opening. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Reduced model on the string: rigid 48.8 g yo-yo, inertia 0.6 mR^2 (estimate), string rolling on a 5 mm effective axle radius. Estimated losses: rub on the halves 1.5e-4 N m; 92% of energy kept through each bottom turnaround. The hand's measured motion drives it, but the string pulls nothing back on the arm. Spin is not drawn. The string is not a collider; touches use fingertip distance. Arms and cradle are rigid PhysX. Riser and cradle are primitives; distractors are SimReady.
scores: Dream-1 run: refused the instruction before acting, nothing scored; demo: 1.0
